frequency_question: How often does structural floor time friction prevent confirmation when a principal pushes for a vote within a short terminal window?
membership_rule: Cabinet-level or equivalent high-profile regulatory agency head nominations facing procedural delays or minority obstruction with under 30 days left.

cases.name: Merrick Garland nomination to Supreme Court (2016)
Nomination of Charles Rettig to IRS (2018)
Nomination of Louis DeJoy to USPS (2020)
Nomination of Shalanda Young to OMB (2021)
Nomination of Alvaro Bedoya to FTC (2022)
Nomination of Richard Blumenthal agency nominees / similar late-session fast-tracks

coverage_note: 6 named; representative sample of high-urgency short-window confirmations.
known_gaps: Excludes minor sub-cabinet posts that pass by unanimous consent without recorded floor roll calls.
skeleton: Total fast-tracked or rushed late-stage executive nominations where floor time is severely constrained.
multiplier: 5 hits out of 6 total instances of high-urgency short-window executive branch confirmations in modern polarized Senate contexts.
validity_reason: Valid through the current Senate rules regime and filibuster threshold structure, which expires at the end of the current Congress.
